A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HAMLET and provide readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably across the substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original drama evaluations, judge–human correlations, PAD strategy and latency measurements, and framework ablations in Tables 1–3 and 10 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original empirical results, including the model leaderboard, human-agreement evaluation, PAD benchmark, latency measurements, and ablation.

M1.justification: The offline planning workflow, online control agents, narrator, and PAD decision procedure remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2, the SFT/DPO training procedures, and all prompt bodies in Tables 11–22 match.

E1.justification: Table 4 drops two explicitly listed custom scenarios: James Bond and Q testing gadgets in Monaco, and Alice meeting characters from multiple literary worlds in Wonderland. The literary sources, English/Chinese coverage, and ten themes remain. This changes documented scenario coverage; the PDFs do not establish whether evaluation runs changed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the leaderboard, judge comparison, PAD benchmark, latency table, and ablation. The same raw-prompted GPT-4o and PAD-disabled HAMLET controls remain.

E3.justification: Both retain the stated 75-item evaluation per language, 30-topic GPT-4o greedy ablation, training hyperparameters, stratified holdouts, and latency-penalty protocol. Table 4 corrects its overlong topic inventory, but the declared evaluation sizes and procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6 retains the same three-configuration ablation and plotted results. Table 6 and Appendix C retain all six cases examining action adjudication, disruptive user inputs, narrative deadlock, and alternative investigative trajectories.

E5.justification: Pearson correlations and average latency reporting are unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-test procedures, and v2 adds none.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. However, the PAD result summary changes from 'top performance across all strategies' with 'zero latency' to 'stable performance' with 'almost zero latency'. The retained tables show PAD Fast at 0.822 versus GPT-4.1-mini at 0.909, and PAD latency at 0.36 seconds.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, decision tuples, and algorithmic expressions are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed; System I/II terminology replaces equivalent numerical notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: topic-driven drama planning, autonomous environmentally interactive actors, PAD, and HAMLETJudge-based evaluation. The claims about the two 8B components are also retained.

C2.justification: The leaderboard discussion newly attributes broad performance benefits to reasoning capabilities and highlights Claude-4-sonnet-Thinking for bilingual practical applications. v1 mainly introduced the comparison and referred to Table 1. Existing latency-comparability caveats and the rationale for excluding Action Tool metrics remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the repository link and code/data/model availability statement, plus the CC BY-NC 4.0 dataset-release statement. This removes access guidance without establishing that resources were withdrawn. Appendix F.1 expands context-field descriptions but omits the separate Environment Description bullet; training settings and operational prompts remain.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Duplicate RAIDEN references are consolidated, and 'Towards Enhanced Immersion and Agency for LLM-based Interactive Drama' receives publication metadata; neither constitutes a change in the underlying cited work.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with limited wording edits and expanded leaderboard and annotation explanations. Sections become numbered, the Annotation Statement moves after the conclusion as an Ethics Statement, and Appendix I replaces author contributions with an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure. Author affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: The document switches from two columns to one, extensively resizing and repositioning figures, tables, algorithms, and prompt boxes. Figure 3 is redrawn horizontally, Table 6 changes row shading and proportions, and Figure 6 gains an expanded caption. Most displays retain their original scientific content.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the overlong topic list, moderates PAD wording to better match Tables 3 and 10, and explains annotation context more clearly. However, removing the repository availability link and dataset license weakens access and reuse guidance. With the core methods and empirical evidence retained, these reporting improvements and reproducibility-information losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
